# OpenModeration — full reference

> AI comment moderation that adapts to each client's rules and use cases, with a team that sets it up with them. For news sites, brands and public bodies. DSA-compliant, hosted in the EU. A Logora product.

OpenModeration moderates the comments on a client's website, Facebook Pages, Instagram professional accounts, YouTube channels and WordPress sites from one console. Every comment is read in context and handled according to the client's own rules: clear violations are hidden automatically, legitimate criticism stays visible, doubtful cases go to the client's team for review, and every decision comes with a written reason and is logged. The OpenModeration team helps each client define its rules and fine-tune them over the first weeks.

- Website: https://www.openmoderation.com (English), https://www.openmoderation.com/fr (French), also /es, /de, /it
- Book a 60-minute call (free, no commitment, live test on your own comments): https://www.openmoderation.com/book-a-call
- Try the live demo without signing up: https://www.openmoderation.com/demo
- Contact: contact@openmoderation.com
- Short version: https://www.openmoderation.com/llms.txt

## Key facts
- **What it is**: a comment moderation service and console (SaaS), not an agency and not a social media management suite.
- **Who it is for**: news sites and newsrooms, brands, retailers and luxury houses, public bodies and local authorities, platforms that host comments.
- **Platforms**: website (API), Facebook Pages, Instagram, YouTube, WordPress. Not supported: TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Discord.
- **AI engine**: OpenModeration runs its own moderation AI, cross-checked by other AI models on delicate cases. It is model-agnostic: when a better or cheaper AI model comes out, it is plugged in quickly with nothing to change for the client, so the moderation follows the progress of the AI market instead of relying on a single frozen in-house algorithm.
- **How decisions are made**: AI reads each comment in context (topic of the article or post, language, irony, coded insults), applies the client's rules, and sends grey-zone cases to human review. Every decision has a written reason.
- **Compliance**: built for the EU Digital Services Act: notice and action (Art. 16), statement of reasons (Art. 17), internal complaints and human review (Art. 20), figures for transparency reports (Art. 15). GDPR, EU hosting.
- **Setup**: connect a page or site, define the rules with the OpenModeration team, test in sandbox mode on real comments without hiding anything, then go live.
- **Scale**: the website states that more than 10 million comments are moderated every day.
- **Company**: OpenModeration is developed by Logora (https://logora.com). Publishers shown on the website as clients: L'Équipe, Challenges, Sud Ouest, actu.fr, Estadão, Südkurier, Egora.
- **Pricing**: free plan up to 1,000 requests a month; Pro €99/month for 10,000 requests; Enterprise on request. Details: https://www.openmoderation.com/pricing

## How it works
1. **Collect**: comments arrive from connected Facebook Pages, Instagram accounts, YouTube channels and WordPress sites, or from any website through the REST API (`POST /v1/moderation`) and webhooks.
2. **Read in context**: AI reads each comment with the title of the article or post, in its language, and recognises irony, coded insults, spam and scams.
3. **Decide with the client's rules**: forbidden words, thresholds per category and rules written in plain language. Clear violations are hidden or rejected automatically, acceptable comments are published, the grey zone goes to review.
4. **Review**: the client's team approves or rejects doubtful cases in one console. Every decision, automatic or human, is logged with its written reason.

## Frequently asked questions
- **Does OpenModeration replace a moderation agency?** It handles the bulk automatically and sends only doubtful cases to people, so many teams use it instead of outsourcing or to reduce agency volumes. See https://www.openmoderation.com/outsourced-moderation
- **Does it remove criticism?** No. Rules distinguish legitimate criticism, which stays visible, from insults, hate, spam and scams.
- **Can we test before going live?** Yes, sandbox mode analyses real comments and shows what would have been decided without hiding anything.
- **Is it DSA-compliant?** It provides the building blocks: user reports handled and logged, a statement of reasons for each decision, human review of contested decisions and exportable figures for transparency reports.
- **Which languages?** Comments are analysed in their own language; the website exists in English, French, Spanish, German and Italian.
- **Does it moderate TikTok?** No. Supported: websites, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, WordPress.
- **Who is behind it?** Logora, a French company (https://logora.com).
